seed_answers.q1: The manual says 'offer the loyalty credit' to any customer threatening to cancel, but it only posts if the account has had no plan change in the last 60 days. The system silently drops it otherwise and the customer calls back angrier. The other thing nobody writes down: a proration dispute is almost never about the math, it's about the cycle date moving. If the plan changed on day 20 of a 30-day cycle, the old plan is billed for 20 days and the new one for 10, plus the new plan's next full month in advance. That 'in advance' part is what people think is a double charge.
seed_answers.q2: New hires reset the billing cycle when a customer asks about proration. They think it 'cleans up' the bill, but it actually generates a second partial charge for the same month, so the next bill looks doubled and the customer disputes it. The second mistake is applying a goodwill credit before the adjustment posts; the credit lands on the old balance and the adjustment then reverses half of it. Rule I taught: never touch the cycle date, and always wait 24 hours after an adjustment before adding any credit.
seed_answers.q3: A customer asked for a retroactive roaming waiver of about $180 after a trip. I checked the toggle history and he had turned data roaming on himself two days before the trip and got the warning text. The waiver policy only covers system errors or a missing warning. I refused, but offered the partial: block the next 7 days of roaming charges if he turned it off now, and I split the $180 across three bills so no single bill was over $60. He accepted. If the warning text had not been sent, I would have waived the whole thing without asking a supervisor.
seed_answers.q4: A family plan account holder moved abroad mid-cycle and wanted only her line moved to an international plan while her kids stayed on the domestic one. The script has no branch for splitting a family plan mid-cycle; it only offers 'change plan for all lines'. I prorated her line for the 14 days remaining, which came to $42.10, kept the kids' lines untouched, and escalated only the roaming portion to the international desk with a note saying do not re-rate the domestic lines. It took 3 calls over 2 weeks but nothing got double-billed.

notes: My own checklist before touching any billing dispute: 1) plan change date vs cycle date 2) roaming toggle history and whether the warning text was sent 3) any credit in the last 24h 4) never reset the cycle 5) if more than 2 lines are affected, write it all down before changing anything.

followup_answers.f1: At day 58 of the 60-day window I do not refuse and I do not promise the credit. I tell the customer the credit is pending review and escalate with a note to apply it on day 61, because the system backdates plan changes on day 61 and the credit posts cleanly then. If you refuse at day 58, the customer cancels; if you apply it, it drops and they call back. The 3-day wait is the only version that works.
followup_answers.f2: For the family plan case: 14 days remaining in the cycle, her line's new plan was $90.21 a month, so the prorated amount was 14/30 of $90.21, which is $42.10. The kids' two lines stayed at $35 each with no re-rating. The roaming part was about $25 of estimated usage and I did not put a number on it in the account; I let the international desk rate it. Three calls total, over 2 weeks, zero double-billing.
